references.text: Pharaoh sought to kill Moses after he had killed the Egyptian. This is the background for why Moses fled to Midian and why God now tells him that those who sought his life are dead.
Pharaoh died, which fulfills what God said to Moses about those who sought his life being dead.
The angel says to Joseph that those who sought the child's life are dead. This is an almost word-for-word parallel to Exodus 4:19, and Matthew presents Jesus as a new Moses.
God commands Jacob to return to his fathers' land, in a similar way that God commands Moses to return to Egypt.
Queen Jezebel sought Elijah's life, just as the Egyptians sought Moses' life. Both prophets had to flee for their lives.
Both verses define a critical turning point in the exodus where God instructs Moses on the route to the promised land.
Both verses mark critical starting points in the history of the exodus: the call to return and the actual departure from Egypt.
